images.title: A lawn with a missing side
images.purpose: Show a lawn of area 72 square m and length 9 m with its breadth marked by a question mark, so that the student sees the missing side as the number that makes 72 when taken 9 times.
images.composition: The lawn on the left with its length, its missing breadth and its area marked, one line of working on the right.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. At the top, centred at x 728 and y 62, the heading A lawn in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (44 px). Left, one rectangle 540 by 480 px (9 units by 8 units of 60 px) at x 200 to 740 and y 170 to 650, filled green #009E73 with a thick dark #2B2B2B outline (6 px) and no inner lines. Above the top side, centred at x 470 and y 118, the label 9 m with a thin dark arrow line 540 px long under it spanning x 200 to 740 at y 150 with an arrowhead at each end; left of the left side, centred at x 130 and y 410, the label ? in dark #1F2937 bold (48 px) with a thin dark arrow line 480 px long spanning y 170 to 650 at x 170 with an arrowhead at each end; in the middle of the rectangle, centred at x 470 and y 410, the label Area 72 square m in white bold sans-serif (44 px). To the right, at x 900, one line of text 72 ÷ 9 = ? at y 330 (44 px, dark #1F2937). In all 1 rectangle, 3 labels on the rectangle and 1 line of text. No other number and no other text anywhere. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any value written for the breadth, or any answer written anywhere in the frame
a rectangle whose sides are not in the ratio 9 to 8
images.takeaway: The breadth is the area divided by the length, and multiplying back checks it.
images.description: A lawn of area 72 square m and length 9 m with the breadth marked ?.
images.context: Concept image for Finding a Missing Side. It follows the idea of the garden question in your maths book (an area and a length are known, the breadth is not) and uses the numbers of this concept's own example.
images.teaching_notes: Let the student ask what number times 9 makes 72 before the division is shown. The slip to watch: multiplying 72 by 9.

image_decisions.why: The lawn with a question mark for the breadth puts the missing side in front of the student.
